result.title: Habitats: A Framework for Open-Ended Evolution of Agent Objectives
result.comment: To be published in the Managing Agents that Manage Agents Workshop on Responsible Use of Meta-Agents at the Fortieth Annual Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (2026)
result.summary: Designing what an agent should optimize can be as difficult as optimizing the agent itself. Existing language-model-based reward-generation methods typically refine objectives for predefined tasks and couple the decision of what to explore with the synthesis of how to implement it, potentially narrowing the resulting behavioral repertoire. We introduce Habitats, a framework for open-ended evolution of executable agent objectives. Habitats maintains a population of reward-policy pairs and evaluates every policy under every population reward, producing a cross-fitness matrix that exposes self-mastery, transfer, and functional diversity. A population-level Planner uses this information to select parent rewards and issue targeted mutation directives, while a separate Mutator translates those directives into validated reward programs. We evaluate Habitats in a discrete Card Sandbox and three continuous-control environments (Cart-Pole, Hopper, and Cheetah) against Independent Generation and Direct Mutation baselines. Across four environments and three random seeds, Habitats achieves the highest macro-averaged final Specialist Quality and Behavioral Diversity, with final diversity reaching 1.8x that of Direct Mutation and 2.5x that of Independent Generation. Finally, across ten downstream objectives unseen during evolution, frozen Habitats policy libraries achieve higher paired win rates than size-matched Direct Mutation and Independent Generation libraries at 10,000 adaptation episodes, while also surpassing task-specific policies trained from scratch for 20,000 episodes. These results suggest that separating population-level planning from reward synthesis enables the discovery of diverse, learnable, and reusable behaviors.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Habitats 框架，让可执行奖励程序与策略共同开放式演化：维护奖励-策略种群并构建交叉适应度矩阵，由独立的 Planner 选择父代奖励并发出变异指令、Mutator 生成经验证的奖励程序，在离散与连续控制环境中提升专精质量与行为多样性。
AI.relevance_reason: 其用交叉适应度矩阵区分「自我掌握」与「迁移」的做法，可能为诊断 latent 推理训练中监督信号与实际复用贡献的对应关系提供评价思路；但该工作针对 RL 奖励演化、不涉及视觉或多模态推理，借鉴价值需核查。
